title: A Multi-Faceted Evaluation Framework for Assessing Synthetic Data Generated by Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces SynEval, an open-source evaluation framework for assessing the fidelity, utility, and privacy of synthetic tabular data (specifically LLM-generated product reviews), tested on outputs from ChatGPT, Claude, and Llama. It combines statistical similarity metrics, downstream ML utility tests, and privacy attacks (e.g., membership inference) into a unified toolkit. title: Multistart Large Neighborhood Search for the liquefied natural gas transportation and trading over long-term time horizons
summary: This preprint develops a Multistart Large Neighborhood Search heuristic combined with a tensor-train optimizer for large-scale LNG transportation and trading problems spanning multi-year planning horizons, handling flexible contracts, fuel consumption, and tank sloshing constraints. The method is evaluated against a linear-programming baseline on historic and artificially generated data, showing substantial profit improvements. Because production instance data could not be disclosed for privacy reasons, the authors generated three artificial test instances using the SDV Python package to mimic the statistical patterns of the real data.

title: NetDiffus: Network Traffic Generation by Diffusion Models through Time-Series Imaging
summary: This paper proposes NetDiffus, a framework that converts one-dimensional network traffic time-series into two-dimensional Gramian Angular Summation Field images and applies diffusion models to synthesize new representative images, improving fidelity and downstream ML task performance over prior GAN-based traffic generators. It evaluates the approach on seven network traffic traces for tasks like fingerprinting, anomaly detection, and classification. title: Not all Jensen-Shannon Divergence Estimators are Equal
summary: This paper studies the measurement problem in estimating the Jensen-Shannon divergence for synthetic tabular data, showing that marginal-based estimators ignore joint dependencies while classifier-based estimators are highly sensitive to protocol choices such as calibration, dimensionality, and class imbalance. The authors derive a closed-form posterior correction for prior shift in classifier-based estimation and release an open-source estimator-aware evaluation tool, validating their analysis on controlled synthetic settings and on the Adult and Intrusion tabular benchmarks. CTGAN is used, alongside a VAE, as one of two generators producing the synthetic data on which the divergence estimators are empirically evaluated.

evidence: "An additional benchmark study was conducted using a tabular generative adversarial network called CTGAN [50]. The CTGAN was trained to generate feasible hull designs... to compare the ability of the CTGAN and the DDPM to generate feasible hulls."

title: In silico generation of synthetic cancer genomes using generative AI
summary: This preprint introduces OncoGAN, a generative AI tool that combines generative adversarial networks and tabular variational autoencoders to produce entirely synthetic cancer genomes -- including somatic point mutations, copy number alterations, and structural variants -- trained on large-scale genomic datasets, aiming to address the scarcity of open, privacy-safe benchmarking data in precision oncology. The work cites the TGAN paper as the basis for its generative modeling approach, and its abstract's mention of 'tabular variational autoencoders' suggests a TVAE-style component within its architecture, though the evidence does not clarify whether the SDV-family library code was run directly or reimplemented by the authors.
evidence: "we have developed OncoGAN, a novel generative AI tool that uses a combination of generative adversarial networks and tabular variational autoencoders to generate realistic but entirely synthetic cancer genomes"; cites_which_sdv_papers lists tgan-2018.
needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether OncoGAN runs the sdv-dev TGAN/TVAE library code directly (api_user) or reimplements the architecture independently (port). Abstract's reference to 'tabular variational autoencoders' alongside a citation to the 2018 TGAN paper (rather than the 2019 CTGAN/TVAE paper) may reflect mis-citation typical in this literature.

title: Single-Model Attribution of Generative Models Through Final-Layer Inversion
summary: This paper proposes FLIPAD, a single-model attribution method that decides whether a sample was produced by a specific generative model, framed as anomaly detection over final-layer-inverted activations solvable as a convex lasso problem. The authors validate FLIPAD across image, tabular, and medical-image generators, including a tabular attribution experiment on wine-quality datasets. CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN were trained using the implementations and default settings provided by the SDV library as the tabular generators whose samples FLIPAD must attribute, alongside KL-WGAN.
evidence: "CTGAN, TVAE, and Copula GAN were trained using the implementations and the default settings provided by the SDV library (Patki et al., 2016)."

title: Six Levels of Privacy: A Framework for Financial Synthetic Data
summary: This paper proposes a six-level hierarchy for classifying synthetic data generation methods by the degree of privacy protection they offer, aimed at financial applications such as data sharing, model training augmentation, and testing. It discusses realism, privacy, and utility trade-offs, surveys privacy attacks, and situates generative techniques including Gaussian copula and GAN-based methods within the levels. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited as an example of a generative technique (Gaussian copula/GAN) used at Level 3 of the hierarchy, without being run or evaluated experimentally.

title: SMOTE-DP: Improving Privacy-Utility Tradeoff with Synthetic Data
summary: This paper proposes SMOTE-DP, a two-stage synthetic data generator pipeline in which a non-differentially-private generator (SMOTE) feeds a differentially private generator, aiming to improve the privacy-utility tradeoff over standard DP mechanisms. The authors prove theoretically and demonstrate empirically that this combination preserves downstream utility while maintaining strong privacy guarantees. CTGAN is cited only in passing, alongside other work, as an example of synthetic data techniques proposed to preserve statistical correlations while hiding personal information, without being run in the experiments.

title: Sparse Density Trees and Lists: An Interpretable Alternative to High-Dimensional Histograms
summary: This paper introduces sparse tree- and list-based generative density estimation models for binary/categorical data, offering an interpretable, visualizable alternative to high-dimensional histograms, with an application to crime modus-operandi analysis. In comparing their methods against Density Estimation Trees (DET), the authors tried pre-processing categorical data with 'the Synthetic Data Vault algorithm from Patki et al. (2016)' as an alternative to one-hot encoding, but found it decreased log-likelihood performance and abandoned it. The original SDV algorithm is run as a rejected preprocessing baseline in a comparison against a competing density-estimation method.

needs: Evidence header claims the citation is bibliographic-only, but quoted passages describe actually running the SDV algorithm as a preprocessing baseline for DET comparison in an appendix; treated the latter as authoritative given the direct quotes.

title: Standardised Metrics and Methods for Synthetic Tabular Data Evaluation
summary: This preprint proposes a unified pipeline of metrics and methods for evaluating synthetic tabular data along resemblance, utility, and privacy dimensions, tested across six healthcare-related datasets using four synthetic tabular data generation approaches. In its background section it surveys prior deep-learning-based synthesis methods, characterising the Synthetic Data Vault as an ensemble of probabilistic graphical and deep-learning techniques and CTGAN as a GAN-based approach for numerical, binary, and categorical data. Both SDV and CTGAN are cited only as prior art in the related-work discussion, without evidence in the available text that either was run in the experiments.
evidence: "Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) [20] synthesise numerical, binary and categorical data efficiently" and "the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) consists of an ensemble approach which combines several probabilistic graphical modelling and Deep Learning (DL) based techniques [21]" -- both appear only in the related-work survey of prior STDG methods.
needs: Full text not obtained; the four STDG approaches actually evaluated are not named in the abstract or citing sentences, so it is unclear whether CTGAN or an SDV synthesizer was actually run as part of the experiments rather than merely cited as background.

title: STaSy: Score-based Tabular data Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes STaSy, a score-based generative model for synthetic tabular data that incorporates a self-paced learning strategy and a fine-tuning step to stabilize denoising score matching training. It benchmarks against seven baselines including CTGAN, TVAE, TableGAN, OCT-GAN, MedGAN, VEEGAN, and RNODE across 15 datasets on sampling quality, diversity, and runtime, and cites Patki et al. (2016)'s recursive Gaussian-copula table modeling as prior work on tabular synthesis. CTGAN and TVAE are run as baseline synthesizers via the SDGym package (github.com/sdv-dev/SDGym), while SDV's original Gaussian copula approach is only cited as related work.

title: Studying the Role of Synthetic Data for Machine Learning-based Wireless Networks Traffic Forecasting
summary: This preprint proposes a novel synthetic-data generation method based on first-order auto-regressive noise statistics for large-scale Wi-Fi traffic forecasting, showing that ML models trained on the generated traces achieve MAE close to real-data-trained models while improving generalization by up to 50%. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is mentioned only in the related-work discussion of structured (tabular/time-series) synthetic data frameworks, describing it as having demonstrated the feasibility of using ML models to replicate statistical properties of real datasets. No SDV code, model, or component is run in the paper's experiments.

title: STUNT: Few-shot Tabular Learning with Self-generated Tasks from Unlabeled Tables
summary: This paper proposes STUNT, a meta-learning framework for few-shot tabular classification that self-generates diverse pseudo-tasks from unlabeled tabular data by clustering randomly selected columns, and introduces an unsupervised validation scheme for hyperparameter search. It is evaluated against self-supervised and unsupervised meta-learning baselines on multiple tabular benchmarks, showing significant performance gains. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of a sophisticated generative model that is cumbersome to train on tabular data, with no experiments run using it.

title: A Survey on Data Collection for Machine Learning: a Big Data -- AI Integration Perspective
summary: A survey of data collection techniques for machine learning, framed from a data management perspective and covering data acquisition, data labeling, and improvement of existing data or models across ML, NLP, vision, and database research communities. It catalogs prior work on synthetic data generation among many other data-acquisition techniques. The Synthetic Data Vault and TGAN are both cited only in the reference list as prior synthetic-data-generation work, with no body-text discussion or use of either.

title: A Survey on Deep Tabular Learning
summary: This is a survey paper reviewing the evolution of deep learning architectures for tabular data, from early fully connected networks through attention-based models (TabNet, SAINT, TabTransformer, FT-Transformer), graph-based and diffusion-based approaches, and pretrained-language-model adaptations. It discusses generative adversarial approaches to tabular data augmentation and class imbalance as part of its related-work coverage. CTGAN is described in prose as introducing mode-specific normalization and a conditional generator to handle non-Gaussian, multimodal, and imbalanced tabular data, but no experiments are run with it.
evidence: "CTGAN addresses several challenges inherent to tabular data, such as handling non-Gaussian and multimodal distributions, by introducing mode-specific normalization and using a conditional generator to manage class imbalance Xu et al. [121]."

title: SurvTimeSurvival: Survival Analysis On The Patient With Multiple Visits/Records
summary: This paper proposes a Transformer-based survival analysis model that handles time-varying covariates and integrates synthetic data generation (via a SurvivalGAN-based technique) to address data sparsity in survival datasets, evaluated on three public medical datasets. The method combines a new Transformer architecture with the SurvTrace model and a SurvivalGAN-style synthetic data component to improve survival prediction accuracy. CTGAN is cited only in the bibliography as prior work on conditional GAN modeling of tabular data, with no evidence it was run in the reported experiments.

title: SynHING: Synthetic Heterogeneous Information Network Generation for Graph Learning and Explanation
summary: This paper proposes SynHING, a framework for generating synthetic heterogeneous information networks (HINs) by identifying motifs from a target HIN and using bottom-up intra- and inter-cluster merge modules with post-pruning, providing ground-truth motifs to benchmark GNN explainer models. The work targets the scarcity of public HIN datasets and evaluation standards for graph explanation methods. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no engagement in the body text.

title: SynLLM: A Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models for Medical Tabular Synthetic Data Generation via Prompt Engineering
summary: This paper presents SynLLM, a modular framework that uses 20 open-source LLMs guided by structured prompts to generate synthetic medical tabular data, evaluating statistical fidelity, clinical consistency, and privacy preservation across three public medical datasets. It proposes four prompt types encoding schema and domain knowledge as an alternative to GAN- or VAE-based generation. CTGAN is cited only in passing in the related-work discussion as a GAN-based method prone to mode collapse and requiring large training data, not run or benchmarked in the experiments.
evidence: "GAN-based methods like CTGAN [41] and MedGAN [22] frequently experience mode collapse and require large amounts of real training data, limiting their utility in privacy-sensitive contexts [15]."

title: Synth-MIA: A Testbed for Auditing Privacy Leakage in Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: This paper introduces Synth-MIA, an open-source Python library implementing 13 membership-inference-attack methods through a scikit-learn-like API, designed to unify and standardize empirical privacy auditing of tabular synthetic data generators. Using this testbed, the authors run the largest tabular synthesis privacy benchmark to date across multiple generator architectures and datasets, showing that higher synthetic data quality correlates with greater privacy leakage and that similarity-based privacy metrics correlate weakly with MIA results. CTGAN and TVAE, both originating from the CTGAN paper, are among the eight generative model architectures evaluated as privacy-leakage subjects, but were implemented via the Synthcity framework rather than SDV's own package.

title: Synthesis of Adversarial DDOS Attacks Using Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: This preprint studies how GAN-synthesized DDoS traffic can be used as adversarial examples to probe and expose weaknesses in machine-learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS). The authors generate tabular attack data with a GAN-based approach, converting categorical fields via one-hot encoding with noise, and evaluate the impact of these synthesized adversarial attacks on IDS detection performance. The paper cites the TGAN work (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) specifically for its categorical one-hot-encoding-with-noise technique, adopting the idea in prose rather than running the SDV-family TGAN implementation itself.
evidence: "Categorical variables, on the other hand, must be converted to binary variables by one hot-encoding with noise [22]" — citing Xu & Veeramachaneni (2018) TGAN for the encoding technique, not running the library.
needs: Full text does not clarify whether the actual GAN implementation used for synthesizing DDoS traffic is TGAN itself, a custom reimplementation, or an unrelated architecture; only the categorical-encoding citation is verifiable.

title: Synthesising Multi-Modal Minority Samples for Tabular Data
summary: This paper proposes a latent-space interpolation framework for oversampling the minority class in imbalanced tabular classification: an autoencoder maps mixed continuous/discrete samples into a dense latent space, interpolation is performed there, and synthetic points are decoded back to the original feature space. The method is evaluated against numerous oversamplers (SMOTE variants, Poly, VAE/AAE/ACAI-based methods, GAN-based methods) across 27 real-world datasets using cover/error and downstream ROC-AUC metrics. CTGAN, run via its open-source implementation (github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN), and TGAN are included as two of many baseline oversamplers, and both are ultimately found to underperform the proposed autoencoder-based approach.
evidence: "CTGAN[27]: A recent generative GAN model specifically designed to handle tabular datasets by conditioning on discrete columns. The open source implementation was used [https://github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN]." CTGAN and TGAN are run as two of many oversampling baselines and both 'performed poorly even when compared to the simple interpolation methods.'

title: Synthesizing Diverse Network Flow Datasets with Scalable Dynamic Multigraph Generation
summary: This paper presents a scalable machine-learning pipeline for generating synthetic dynamic multigraph network-flow (netflow) datasets, combining a stochastic Kronecker graph generator for topology, a tabular GAN for edge features, and an XGBoost model for graph alignment, with new metrics to evaluate accuracy and diversity of synthetic graphs versus prior large-scale graph generation methods. CTGAN is used as the feature-generation stage, trained to learn edge-feature distributions with mode-specific normalization applied to continuous values and one-hot encoding for discrete ones, and sampled to produce synthetic netflow features overlaid onto the generated graph structure.
evidence: "Feature generation employs a Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) model [18] to learn the distribution of the edge features... we apply the mode-specific normalization proposed in CTGAN to the continuous values... CTGAN is trained to learn the feature distributions, from which we sample M times."
needs: Not clear whether the sdv-dev/ctgan package was actually run or the authors reimplemented CTGAN themselves; no library name, import, or hyperparameter names are given, so integration mechanism (api_user vs port) is ambiguous.

title: Synthesizing real-world distributions from high-dimensional Gaussian Noise with Fully Connected Neural Network
summary: This paper proposes DiMSO (Distribution Mapping with Shuffled Optimization), a fully-connected neural network that maps high-dimensional Gaussian noise to a target tabular distribution, combined with PCA for privacy and two novel Wasserstein/covariance-based loss functions. It is evaluated against traditional and deep-learning generators (SMOTE, Synthpop, TabDiff, CTGAN, TVAE) across 25 tabular datasets on distributional similarity, privacy, and downstream classification utility. CTGAN and TVAE, drawn from the synthetic data vault library, are run as deep-learning baseline generators throughout the comparison, and Gaussian Copula from the same library is discussed as a traditional statistical alternative.

title: Synthesizing Tabular Data using Generative Adversarial Networks

The paper is the founding work for the 'tgan' component of the SDV family, authored by the MIT DAI Lab researchers behind SDV, and its citation of the earlier SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016) situates TGAN within that same synthetic-data ecosystem rather than reporting any use of SDV's software.
